clue.text: Take off garment I'd first put on upside down

indicators.note: the piece from I'd is placed ahead of the garment
in a down clue, turning a piece upside down reads its letters from the bottom up

parts.note: I'd is written ID without the apostrophe
a vest is an undergarment

explanation.surface: Someone dressing clumsily, pulling a garment on the wrong way up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upside down' turns ID into DI, which goes first before VEST.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip or deprive someone of something, especially clothing or power, is a direct synonym of taking it off.

clue.text: Casting is one of his jobs in the studio

definitions.text: Casting is one of his jobs in the studio

parts.words: Casting is one of his jobs in the studio
parts.note: reads like a film or theatre director choosing actors, but the casting is of metal in bronze, done by an artist in his studio

explanation.walkthrough: 'Casting' and 'studio' suggest film-making; the studio is an artist's workshop and the casting is pouring bronze.
explanation.definitionFit: A maker of statues and carvings casts bronze figures in a workshop, so the description fits this artist.

definitions.meaning: a member of a Native American people of the Great Plains
uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker, so the question mark invites a word for one involved in pawning goods

explanation.walkthrough: 'uncle' is old British slang for a pawnbroker, the one who holds pledged goods; the playful word means one who takes a pawn.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pawnee are a Plains nation, and the word also reads as someone to whom a pledge is pawned.

clue.text: A long time since Agnes lost heart with an attempt

indicators.note: the name Agnes drops its central letter, its heart

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, a
to have a go is to make an attempt

explanation.surface: Agnes became discouraged after trying something a long time ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost heart' removes N, the middle of AGNES, leaving AGES.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a great while back in the past, matching a long time since.

parts.note: the end is the finish
to have an ear for music is musical ability

explanation.surface: A list of a performer's qualities: charm, polish and a good ear.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone is to win their affection, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Team with genuine line-up of stars

indicators.note: in this down clue the two pieces are lined up one above the other

parts.note: a team is a side in sport
genuine means real

explanation.surface: A team of authentic stars lined up for a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line-up' tells you to stack the pieces in order; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronomical adjective meaning relating to or measured by the fixed stars.

definitions.meaning: to fire a gun or to dismiss someone from a job
to unload cargo or a weapon

explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both firing a weapon or an employee and unloading a cargo or burden.

parts.note: suggests a dentist prising jaws apart, but the teeth are those of a fastener on clothing

explanation.walkthrough: The teeth belong to a zip fastener, not a mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling the slider of a fastener separates its interlocked metal or plastic teeth, opening it.

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Kitchen helpers in an army mess hall dish out second helpings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is part of the fodder, not a link; 'mess' alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To refill or restock, giving another helping, is what supplying seconds means.

indicators.note: the abbreviation for 'for example' is placed inside the bet

parts.note: to speculate is to bet or gamble
EG is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Gambling on farm produce futures, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: An old verb meaning to father or bring about offspring, so to produce.

parts.note: an is the form of 'a' before a vowel

indicators.note: a reflection shows the article's letters back to front

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A woman writes a thoughtful, introspective piece.
explanation.walkthrough: AN plus NA, its mirror image; 'She's writing' is surface dressing around the definition 'She'.
explanation.definitionFit: A common girl's name, standing for any female person, as crosswords often do with she.

clue.text: Representation of body height not right

indicators.note: R, the abbreviation for right, is left out

parts.note: a person's height is their stature

explanation.surface: A figure drawing got the body's height wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved or cast figure is a sculpted representation of a human body.

clue.text: Supports attempts to back horse to come first

indicators.note: the reversed horse is placed before the attempts
the word for a horse is read backwards

parts.note: a nag is an old horse
tries are attempts

explanation.surface: A punter's betting tips: tries to back a horse to win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses NAG to GAN; 'back' and 'come first' borrow racing betting language.
explanation.definitionFit: Frameworks spanning rails or roads that hold up cranes or signals are structural supports.

clue.text: Player inserts key in a lock

parts.note: C is a musical key
a lock of hair is a tress

explanation.surface: Someone putting a key into a door lock.
explanation.walkthrough: The lock is of hair, not a door; C goes inside TRESS after A.
explanation.definitionFit: A female performer on stage or screen is a player in the theatrical sense.
Informally the word means mad, and it also names savoury dry biscuits often eaten with cheese.

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to husband resources is to use them sparingly

explanation.walkthrough: 'husband' is a verb here, meaning to conserve.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to rescue from harm and to keep resources back thriftily.

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, so his cry is literally the call of a cat, which names a jeer

explanation.walkthrough: Tom is a male cat, so his cry is a cat's call; the word names a whistle of derision.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrill whistle or shout of disapproval from an audience is a jeer, a cry of derision.

definitions.meaning: short set prayers in the Christian liturgy

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means gathers together, and the noun names short liturgical prayers said on set days.

clue.text: Where to find fruit or tea on the way

indicators.note: in this down clue the tea sits on top of the way

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: Planning a walk: pick fruit or stop for tea along the route.
explanation.definitionFit: A plantation of fruit trees is exactly the place where fruit is grown and found.

indicators.note: arrangements here means rearranging the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Talk through and approve the travel plans.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb meaning to debate or consider something thoroughly, so to discuss.

clue.text: Eastern garment for the weekend, a loud colour

parts.note: the end of the word week is K
F is forte, the musical direction for loud
tan is a brown colour

explanation.surface: Choosing a bright, loud robe to wear at the weekend.
explanation.definitionFit: A long loose tunic worn in the Middle East and Central Asia is an Eastern garment.

clue.text: May be counted as a hazard in headquarters

definitions.text: May be counted as a hazard in headquarters

parts.words: May be counted as a hazard in headquarters
parts.note: reads like a security risk at a military base, but the count is a daily airborne reading and the head is where hay fever strikes

explanation.walkthrough: Weather forecasts give a count of this airborne dust, which irritates the head; 'May' hints at the season.
explanation.definitionFit: Plant dust is measured daily in a count and causes hay fever, a hazard to noses and heads.

parts.note: not the sea creature but a fish among the stars, a zodiac constellation

explanation.walkthrough: The star sign is depicted as two fishes, so it is a fish in the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac constellation shown as a pair of fishes is literally a fish among the stars.

parts.note: sounds like knitting or sailing, but it is the stage direction sending the cast of actors off

explanation.walkthrough: Latin for 'they go out', the stage direction ordering the actors to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin stage direction tells several actors to leave, literally ordering the cast off stage.

clue.text: 50s' music, with the French missing the boat

indicators.note: the French article is absent from the music

parts.note: skiffle was a folk-blues style popular in 1950s Britain
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French band playing 1950s music missed the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: SKIFFLE was a 1950s British craze using washboards and homemade instruments; removing LE leaves SKIFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A small light rowing or sailing boat.

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
hastened means hurried, raced

explanation.surface: Lots of runners competed but lost the race.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone subdued and humbled by defeat or rebuke has been beaten down.

indicators.note: the leader of Daily is its opening letter

parts.note: to have read a subject is to have studied it

explanation.surface: A newspaper editorial studied with alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' also means a newspaper editorial, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Fear and apprehension are synonyms for alarm.

clue.text: Stopping for breather in a boxing arena

indicators.note: the breather goes inside the a-plus-ring combination

parts.note: a boxing ring
a breather is a rest

explanation.surface: A boxer taking a breather in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrest something is to halt it, so the participle means stopping.
